---
applyTo: "packages/genui/server/**,packages/genui/playground/src/pages/chat/**"
---

Treat TypeSafe Jev as an A2UI and OpenUI decision/composition provider, not an OpenAI-compatible language model. Resolve its server-owned connection from a `provider: "typesafe"` entry. Use only that selected Jev model for every composition stage. Never require, invoke or fall back to another model, even for content preparation. A TypeSafe-only configuration must work.

A2UI and OpenUI Create also support a complete request-scoped Jev connection through Custom API key: select the fixed TypeSafe Jev endpoint `https://api.typesafe.ai/v1`, default model `jev-latest`, and use the supplied API key. Resolve this endpoint to the evaluation provider before the language-model path, independently of server configuration and model aliases. Allow only the exact endpoint and optional trailing slash; keep it out of the OpenAI-compatible endpoint list and other protocols/Bench. Disable redirects on the custom evaluator fetch, preserve cancellation and request diagnostics, and never mix custom and server-owned connection fields. Do not persist custom credentials, model or endpoint. Verify Create and action JSON/SSE paths with deterministic mocks and no server model configuration. Forward the shared Design option through A2UI HTTP normalization for both custom and configured models.

Derive components and property choices from the active Catalog, user input and existing UI/state. Do not introduce business recipes, fixed sample datasets, a quoted-heading requirement or provider-specific UI descriptions. Jev chooses finite options; it does not invent free-form text or missing data. Preserve the shared prompt suggestions and Design Guidance control across models.

Harvest explicit JSON values, quoted copy and complete phrases before generating bounded word fragments. Rank current requests and matching JSON fields ahead of older or unrelated values. Normally offer up to 32 property values, expanding to at most 96 for complete supplied content, bindings and Catalog alternatives; reserve space for unquoted multilingual fragments. Preserve exact authorized image URLs and never include resolved input values in binding descriptions. Distinguish synthetic empty placeholders from explicit empty values and Catalog enums/consts.

Omit an absent optional property's question only when its choices are all synthetic placeholders. Keep required properties and optional visual/behavioral alternatives available. Deduplicate equivalent values, including a retained value already in the candidate list, so single-choice evaluation stays local. The existing component-retention phase may explicitly select `preserve` to reuse optional properties and omissions on an existing node and its fixed children; movable descendants decide independently. Required content is still evaluated. Never infer preservation from language-specific keywords or let it bypass current host-resource authorization.

Select components, configure properties and arrange the tree using bounded batches of Jev questions. Batch direct structural parent proposals, excluding each unit's own descendants; do not use independently chosen layer numbers that prevent otherwise valid nesting. Install valid proposals locally in dependency order. For a cycle or an actual depth overflow, offer replacement edges to already placed containers and let Jev resolve only the conflicting portion. Batch independent conflicts; every resolution must make progress without modifying retained edges. Treat each moving component with its fixed children/slots/template scope and parent-preserved descendants as one unit and include its full height in parent depth checks. Batch leaf placement after the structural tree is resolved, then order actual sibling groups. Publish only the completed, validated layout, never temporary root staging. Validate the combined graph, component budget, depth and Catalog. Preserve completed evaluation usage on invalid choices, layout failures and cancellation. Use the selected Jev prices; no automatic provider retries or fallback are allowed.

Select layout preservation in the existing retention question, without a separate model phase. `keep_layout` and `preserve_layout` retain a node's parent and relative sibling order; `reorder` and `reorder_preserve` retain only its parent. The variants containing `preserve` also reuse optional properties. Existing `keep` and `preserve` allow reparenting, and new nodes receive fresh placement decisions. Movable descendants decide independently; a descendant whose parent is retained travels with that parent's placement unit. Never reuse an id from the previous snapshot for replacement content. Ask ordering questions only for nodes allowed to change position, bound positions to actual siblings, and resolve singleton groups locally. Ordering depends on final parent choices and must not share their batch. Merge repositioned nodes into unchanged siblings in their original children-array order. If changed siblings choose the same position, allocate their relative order through explicit Jev decisions, batching independent ties; never silently use Catalog/component enumeration as the tie breaker.

Preserve compound and named children, repeating template scopes, ids and current state during editing. Do not send entered input values or action context to the evaluator; share display copy and binding paths/types only. Server-dispatched events can change UI composition but cannot claim external operations occurred. Use shared image/link source policies.

Distinguish new staged nodes from existing layout in every layout batch. Temporary root placement and Catalog enumeration order are not user-authored parent/order constraints. Only attach existing parent/position metadata to ids from the previous snapshot. Include fixed-child ownership, structural proposals, and actual sibling groups during ordering so compound labels and content slots remain visible across batches. Schema-valid trees can still violate requested grouping; deterministic topology tests do not establish live-model semantic accuracy.

Do not offer synthesized empty placeholders for required display properties, or new components whose required display content has no remaining candidate. RadioGroup options are its `items` data, not component `children`; an empty placeholder array does not fulfill a requested option list. Preserve explicitly supplied empty values, Catalog enum/const values, valid bindings and initial empty bound input `value` state. Apply the same rule to component availability and property choices so supplied nonempty arrays cannot fall back to a synthesized empty array.

Batch new Text copy with owner/slot, role, ordinal and the complete copy-target plan in every batch. Component counts exclude automatically created compound labels and slots and describe the current interaction state. After layout fixes the final parent scopes, identify only the duplicate new literal Text siblings that snapshot cleanup would remove. Give each such node one sequential allocation from unused copy candidates or an explicit omission; never retry provider failures or re-evaluate unaffected text. Remove omitted nodes and child references before the final snapshot. Preserve existing text, binding/template content, fixed action labels, different styles and repeated copy in separate containers. Remove new empty container subtrees only after layout, when their intended contents have been placed.

Resolve single-option Jev questions locally before batching. Send at most 32 remaining questions per evaluation, with at most two concurrent batches within one independent phase. Keep conflicting-copy allocation, structural conflict resolution and ordering dependencies sequential. On failure or cancellation, stop queued work, abort sibling calls and await active requests so all returned usage is retained before finalizing the response. Test concurrency and cancellation with controlled promises, not live model timing.

Record Jev diagnostics at the actual provider-call boundary, with an invocation-local request index, phase, question/choice counts, duration, normalized per-call usage and terminal status. Forward bounded metadata through `model` SSE events in both Create and action streams into the shared Agent interaction timeline. Do not count locally resolved questions, composition snapshots or SSE chunks as model requests. Keep the total independent of timeline eviction and include it in Copy details; do not persist interaction traces. Keep per-call usage nested under the diagnostic response so it cannot replace the turn's aggregate billing usage. Never expose raw state, instructions, choice text, selected content, credentials, upstream model identifiers/URLs or provider error bodies in these diagnostics.

Filter Image.url candidates by renderer semantics and the shared image source policy before asking Jev to select components or properties. Check the resolved value of offered image bindings without exposing it to the evaluator. Descriptive text and empty strings are not image sources. When no valid source exists, omit new Image components and compose the remaining content; preserve valid existing images during edits.

Keep Jev out of other protocols and Bench. `/models?protocol=a2ui` and `/models?protocol=openui` may expose `composition: true`, never credentials or upstream ids. Complete custom provider requests must not inherit Jev credentials. Test the existing Create SSE route with deterministic TypeSafe-only mocks, cancellation, retained usage and a deployment with no text model.

Offer McpApp only when the host supplies a resolved resource through the server-only `A2UIChatOptions.hostedMcpApps` capability. Require a registered ui:// resource URI, a usable bundle URL and renderer/input data; validate any supplied web bundle URL too. Do not authorize resources from prompts, arbitrary Catalog entries, conversation data/history or public HTTP fields. Select each resource's native URL, optional web URL and render data atomically; expose only its title/URI to Jev. Rebind retained apps to current host resources. Without resources, remove prior McpApp nodes and repair affected child references/required slots before composing a new snapshot.

OpenUI Jev must compose the native headless library from `createOpenUiPromptLibrary`, not translate an A2UI snapshot or invoke another model. Share finite-value harvesting, bounded evaluation, and tree/layout algorithms under `agent/common`; keep protocol-specific schema/slot adapters separate. OpenUI Card uses children, Button uses label, Buttons accepts only Button children, and Modal/Tabs keep their native slots. Serialize with `jsonToOpenUI`, preserve referenced runtime statements through `mergeStatements`, and parse the complete result with the same active library before publishing any DSL. Preserve declared state and input names on edits, update entered values locally, and strip raw OpenUI action context from model requests. Only generate local input state and assistant actions; do not invent Query/Mutation tools. Preserve existing authorized runtime expressions on follow-up edits. OpenUI Create and action continuations use `/openui/stream`, the same demo prompts/Design setting, and the shared diagnostics/custom connection policy.

Keep protocol Schema normalization, component/slot specifications, binding encodings, resource filters and component availability in each protocol's `jev-candidates.ts`. Build candidates after restoring current state locally. Delegate harvesting, property ranking, explicit/default/placeholder handling, deduplication and candidate budgets to `agent/common/jev-values.ts`. Candidate construction stays local and never calls the evaluator.

Implement shared Jev capabilities in this repository without introducing `ai.experimental_evaluate`. Keep direct TypeSafe provider calls, bounded phase scheduling, single-choice resolution and actual-call diagnostics in `agent/common/jev-evaluator.ts`. Use `agent/common/jev-composition.ts` for design/retention context, component-count and retention questions, fixed-slot retention and property-question/value application. Keep tree constraints and layout planning shared. Protocol composers own native restoration, root/slot construction, actions, state, copy cleanup and final validation/serialization; do not translate OpenUI through A2UI or copy generic policies between them.

Use `service/common/jev-composition.ts` for the invocation-scoped connection, 60-second deadline, cancellation, diagnostic forwarding, aggregate usage, sanitized errors, single-consumption stream and finalization. Protocol services supply validated artifact text plus their wire chunks. Retain completed usage and the last validated artifact on failure; reject finalization of failed or partially consumed streams. Closing a stream must abort its invocation. Keep protocol framing and publication policy outside the shared runtime. Test the shared policies with deterministic values and controlled generators alongside native A2UI/OpenUI integration tests.
